newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CLOSED-END FUNDS NAV DISCOUNT DROPS IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CLOSED-END FUNDS NAV DISCOUNT DROPS IN JULY.

text.p: Greece's 16 closed-end investment funds listed on the Athens bourse had a market capitalisation of 168.8 billion drachmas at the end of July, up from 155.8 billion a month earlier, the Association of Institutional Investors said.

Their shares traded at an average 0.6 percent discount to total NAV in end-July, the association said. They had traded at a 6.3 percent discount a month earlier and a 7.4 premium at the end of May 1997.
The funds' total NAV amounted to 169.9 billion drachmas at the end of July, versus 166.3 billion on June 30.
Statistics showed five funds -- Alpha, Hellenic, National, Piraeus and Ionian -- were trading at a premium to their net asset value (NAV) in end-July, up from three a month earlier.
The share performance of four funds -- National, Piraeus, Exelixi and Ergo -- managed to better the bourse's benchmark index in the seven months to July 31.
The Athens stock exchange's general index started the year at 954.54 and gained 643.8 points or 67.45 percent to 1,598.34 points at end-July.
The funds allocated more assets into Greek equities and fixed-income securities in July, reducing their drachma cash and money instrument positions.
* market cap, premium/discount to NAV based
